diagnostic_evidence.quote: For  functions $\phi \in H^{2}(\Omega)+\Vhq$, boundedness holds in the following sense:

issues.failure_explanation: The declared domain includes functions whose gradients have no face traces, whereas the SIP formula integrates such traces over interior faces. For example, a broken H1 function behaving like x^(3/4) near a face in one dimension has no finite normal-derivative trace there. The later analysis uses the substantially narrower, well-defined classes Vh and H2(Ω)+Vh.

failure_location.quote: we employ the \emph{Symmetric Interior Penalty discontinuous Galerkin} (SIP-dG) form $\asip: H^1(\triangles) \times H^1(\triangles) \rightarrow \R$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the SIP arguments to an appropriate piecewise H2 space, or to H2(Ω)+Vh, with the coefficient trace assumptions used later.
issues.overall_effect: The asserted functional domain is invalid, although the actual discrete and sufficiently regular exact arguments used later are admissible.
issues.title: The SIP form is not defined on the declared broken H1 domain
issues.why_classification: This is a local domain correction that preserves the numerical method and every subsequent substantive application of the form.

issues.failure_explanation: The stated condition n>d/ell does not imply the n>d/2 condition needed for this Hn-based uniform estimate. For example, d=3, n=1, ell=4 is admitted. On a fixed element, smooth unit-height bumps with shrinking support have H1 norms tending to zero, but their uniform approximation error by fixed-degree polynomials cannot tend to zero.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the Hn-based L-infinity estimate separately under n>d/2, leaving the W^{n,ell} estimate under its own condition.
issues.overall_effect: The auxiliary lemma asserts an invalid parameter range. Its later L-infinity applications use n=q+1>d/2 and are not invalidated by this root.
issues.title: The L-infinity interpolation estimate lacks its Hn regularity threshold
issues.why_classification: The missing regularity condition is standard and local, and all substantive downstream uses already satisfy it.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: For $n-\frac{d}{\ell}>0$ and $0 \leq i \leq n \leq q+1$, the following bounds hold:

issues.failure_explanation: The admitted case d=1, ell=2, n=1 provides only H1 regularity, which does not define the normal-gradient traces in the starred seminorm. On K=(0,1), phi=x^(3/4) is H1, but subtracting a polynomial does not remove its unbounded derivative at zero. Thus the left-hand side need not even be defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require sufficient gradient-trace regularity for this estimate; n≥2 suffices for the integer-order cases used in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The starred estimate is false in part of its stated range. The later uses with n=q+1≥2 remain available.
issues.title: The starred interpolation estimate is asserted without gradient-trace regularity
issues.why_classification: A separate local regularity condition fixes the estimate without changing any later approximation rate or dimension-degree regime.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof uses L-infinity stability of the interpolant and then treats the contribution of the exact pressure as r with coefficient one. Stability supplies a constant C_I, not necessarily one for higher-degree interpolation. Consequently the displayed estimates give C_I r+o(1), which need not be below one when r is close to one. Refining h does not eliminate that factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the interpolation error estimate instead: bound ||kappa I_h p||∞ by ||kappa p||∞ plus O(h^{q+1-d/2}). This leaves r with coefficient one and makes the remaining terms vanish with h.
issues.overall_effect: The continuation proof does not establish the acoustic theorem throughout its stated non-degenerate pressure range.
issues.title: Interpolation stability does not preserve the exact non-degeneracy margin
issues.why_classification: The source already supplies the needed interpolation estimate and uses this sharper comparison for the initial pressure, so a short local replacement preserves the full theorem.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The functions  $\fhp \in  L^2(0,T; \Vhq)$, $\gAh \in L^2(0,T; \VGh)$, and $\fhu \in L^2(0,T; \Vhq)$, $\ghin \in L^2(0,T; \VGinh)$ are assumed to approximate
the local version of the Picard--Lindelöf theorem~\cite[Problem 7.1.3]{picardlindelofp105} yields the local existence of a unique solution

issues.failure_explanation: The loads are only L2 in time, so the asserted time continuity and boundedness required by this classical ODE argument are unavailable. Take kappa=0 and spatially constant p(t)=t^(7/4), with f_p=p_tt and g_abs=alpha p_t, and choose the discrete loads exactly. All stated regularity and accuracy assumptions hold, but testing with the constant function rules out any C2 solution at t=0 because p_tt is unbounded there. Thus the set defining t_h* can be empty. The concentration equation has the analogous obstruction to C1 regularity.

failure_location.quote: Under the assumptions of Theorem \ref{thm: wellposedness nonlin}, $\thh>0$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retain L2 loads but formulate the pressure solution in H2(0,T;Vh) and concentration in H1(0,T;Vh), impose the equations almost everywhere, and adapt the local existence and continuation steps to the Carathéodory ODE setting. Amend the corresponding bootstrap definition and theorem regularity clauses.
issues.overall_effect: The classical local existence, positive bootstrap interval, and C2/C1 well-posedness claims are false for allowed temporal loads.
issues.title: L2-in-time loads do not yield the claimed classical semi-discrete solutions
issues.why_classification: This requires a contained replacement of the ODE existence argument and weaker temporal regularity promises, but preserves the admitted loads, spatial rates, and overall proof architecture.

issues.failure_explanation: For the advertised case d=2, q=1, estimating I_h p_tt-p_tt in L2 at order h uses n=1 and ell=2. Then n-d/ell=0, violating the interpolation lemma's strict hypothesis. The additional L-infinity assumption on p_tt does not supply the missing spatial derivative regularity or a uniform H1-based nodal interpolation estimate.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the already introduced L2 projection in the pressure error splitting, establish its H^q approximation and L-infinity/trace bounds, and retain the resulting initial-error terms. issues.overall_effect: The pressure defect bound, and hence the asserted convergence proof for linear elements in two dimensions, is unsupported under the stated Xp regularity.
issues.title: The pressure defect estimate applies interpolation outside its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: Preserving the original regularity regime requires a contained projection argument and associated estimates; simply retaining nodal interpolation requires a substantive additional regularity assumption.

Small positive SIP penalties can leave the stiffness form indefinite, so coercive control of the error seminorm cannot be inferred merely by reducing h.

issues.title: Acoustic coercivity is invoked without a sufficient penalty assumption

issues.failure_explanation: The local existence argument gives membership in A_h only on its initial local interval. The definition of t_h* requires an error bound at a single endpoint and does not require the solution to remain in A_h throughout the preceding interval. Nor is a quantitative choice of C0 given that would imply that membership. The positive kinetic-energy coefficient used here is therefore an unestablished premise.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define a genuine first-exit interval requiring membership in A_h and the bootstrap bound for every preceding time. Work below its supremum, use the uniform bounds to obtain an endpoint limit, and then prove both inequalities are strict there before continuing.
issues.overall_effect: The uniform energy estimate assumes the non-degeneracy needed for the continuation argument rather than securing it on the interval where the estimate is applied.
issues.title: Non-degeneracy on the bootstrap interval is assumed without being established
issues.why_classification: This is a standard local correction to the stopping-time construction within the continuation architecture already developed in the source.

issues.failure_explanation: Only the acoustic initial data are required to approximate their exact counterparts. The concentration initial value remains arbitrary in Vh, while the proof drops its initial error after integration. With exact p=u=0, zero sources, v=0, and u_h(0)=1, all stated initial-data requirements are met but the claimed error is already |Ω| at t=0, independently of h.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require u_h(0)=I_h u_0, or at least ||u_h(0)-u_0||L2=O(h^q), and retain the corresponding initial-energy term in the proof.
issues.overall_effect: The concentration error estimate and the subsequent overshoot estimate fail for admitted discrete initial concentrations.
issues.title: Concentration convergence has no initial approximation hypothesis
issues.why_classification: This standard local initialization condition preserves the concentration method, all rates, and the class of regular exact initial data.
